title: A wake never waits on a shim lock under the bus's hold lock
intention: Waking a shim never waits on another shim's lock while holding the bus's one hold lock, so a busy shim cannot deadlock or stall any other wake.
why: Telos via the bus charter (mail arrives; a slow answer blocks only its own device's traffic, decision 8 in server.py's per-shim-lock comment) and Law 3: measured 2026-10-18 by a scratch-bus proof, the cycle hangs both threads indefinitely and every wake on the bus queues behind one busy shim.
traces_to: Telos via the bus charter (mail arrives; a slow answer blocks only its own device's traffic, decision 8 in server.py's per-shim-lock comment) and Law 3: measured 2026-10-18 by a scratch-bus proof, the cycle hangs both threads indefinitely and every wake on the bus queues behind one busy shim.
how: In BusProcess, _hold_lock guards only the roster lookup or shim construction in hold_name/hold_class; _wire runs after it is released, and _wire re-checks 'already wired' under the shim's own lock so two concurrent wakes wire once. A proof on a scratch bus drives the two-thread cycle through op_verbs and post, reads red today (measured 2026-10-18: both threads still waiting at 10s; an unrelated wake waits 2s+ behind a busy shim) and green after. Builder notes: Questions a Haiku builder would need, answered. (a) What changes? Only cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py, three spots in BusProcess. (b) hold_name: keep `with self._hold_lock: shim = self.roster.shim_for(name)`, then dedent the `if shim is None: raise LookupError(...)`, the `if wire: self._wire(shim)` and the `return shim` out of the with block. (c) hold_class: dedent only the final `if wire: self._wire(shim)` and `return shim` out of the with block. Construction and _by_spec stay inside. (d) _wire: replace the first check with `if self._is_wired(shim.device_id): return`. Inside `with self._holding(shim.device_id):`, first re-check `if self._is_wired(shim.device_id): return`, then call shim._wire_delivery(), self._wired.add(...), and the existing hook-wrapping block, all indented inside the with. (e) Add the method `def _is_wired(self, device_id: str) -> bool: return device_id in self._wired and device_id in self.bus._delivery_hooks` right after _wire. (f) The proof is already written and committed. The builder only runs it. Expect 1 of 3 before the change and 3 of 3 after.
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_wake_never_waits_under_the_hold_lock.py has three teeth. (1) A cold verb on X whose handler mails a sleeping Y, while X's own mail arrives, finishes inside 10s. (2) While X is busy, mail to an unrelated sleeper Z is taken inside 2s. (3) A sleeper woken from two threads starts its device once, and both envelopes are taken. Measured 2026-10-18 against today's server.py: 1 of 3, teeth 1 and 2 red. All bus proofs stay green. Horizon: PROVED; the reverted server.py reds teeth 1 and 2 in the hollow reading.
watchme: none, because the outcome is a structural property measured by the proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_wake_never_waits_under_the_hold_lock.py, which reruns at every bin/cairn test --seal touching server.py; a live recurrence would show as a request timing out in the live troubles lane printed by bin/cmd/slate
